title: Telling the Time in Chinese: 点, 分 and 半 (HSK 1)
description: How to tell the time in Chinese: 几点 questions, 点, 分 and 半, why it is 两点 not 二点, where the time goes in a sentence, and HSK 1 examples.
h1: Telling the Time: 点, 分 and 半
lede: Chinese tells the time with a number and 点 (diǎn) for the hour, 分 (fēn) for the minutes and 半 (bàn) for half past. The time always comes before the verb, so "I get up at seven" is 我七点起床.

paras: To ask the time, use 几点 (jǐ diǎn, "what time"). To answer, put the number in front of 点. You don't need 是 ("to be"): 现在两点 simply means "It's two o'clock now."
The most common mistake is 二点. For two o'clock, always say 两点 (liǎng diǎn). For twelve o'clock, it is still 十二点, because 二 is only replaced when it stands alone before 点.

examples.py: Xiànzài liǎng diǎn, bú shì shí'èr diǎn.

paras: Minutes come after the hour: hour + 点 + minutes + 分. For half past, add 半 after 点: 八点半 is half past eight. 半 never goes before the hour.

For minutes under ten, people often add 零 (líng, "zero"): 十点零五分. In everyday speech, 分 is often dropped when the minutes are ten or more, so 七点二十 means 7:20. You may also hear 一刻 (yí kè, "a quarter"), but it is not an HSK 1 word.

examples.py: Wǒmen jiǔ diǎn shí fēn shàngkè.
examples.en: Our class starts at ten past nine.

examples.py: Xiànzài shí diǎn líng wǔ fēn.
Tā wǎnshang qī diǎn èrshí dào jiā.
examples.en: He gets home at 7:20 in the evening.

sections.h2: Where the time goes in a sentence
paras: The time goes before the verb, usually straight after the subject: 我早上七点起床. Saying 我起床早上七点, following English word order, is a very common learner mistake.

Chinese does not use "am" and "pm". Instead, put a word such as 早上, 上午, 中午, 下午 or 晚上 before the time. When there is a day as well, go from big to small: day, then part of the day, then the hour, as in 明天上午十一点.

examples.en: I get up at seven in the morning.
What time do you finish work?

examples.py: Wǒ xiàwǔ wǔ diǎn bàn xiàbān.
examples.en: I finish work at half past five in the afternoon.

examples.zh: 明天上午十一点，你有时间吗？
examples.py: Míngtiān shàngwǔ shíyī diǎn, nǐ yǒu shíjiān ma?
examples.en: Are you free at eleven tomorrow morning?

sections.h2: A time vs how long: 点 or 小时, 分 or 分钟
paras: 点 and 分 give a point in time: 两点 is two o'clock. For how long something lasts, use 个小时 (ge xiǎoshí, hours) and 分钟 (fēnzhōng, minutes): 两个小时 is two hours, 二十分钟 is twenty minutes.
A length of time goes after the verb, not before it: 我学习了两个小时 means "I studied for two hours".

examples.zh: 我今天学习了两个小时。
examples.py: Wǒ jīntiān xuéxí le liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.en: I studied for two hours today.

examples.zh: 我昨天晚上睡了八个小时。
examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.en: I slept for eight hours last night.

examples.py: Tā kàn le èrshí fēnzhōng diànshì.
examples.en: He watched TV for twenty minutes.
